center?

optional center?: Object3D<Object3DEventMap>;

Defined in: experiments/star-field/engine/types.ts:664

Body-system center — the group that carries the orbit radius (position.x = def.orbit) and hosts everything that must share the body's location but NOT its orientation: the axis-lock group, the bare mesh, satellite pivots and constellation swarms. It never rotates itself, so children orbit the body's center in the pivot frame instead of inheriting surface spin or lock counter-rotation. For orbiting bodies this is also the eccentric-orbit target — frame.ts rewrites its position.x with the conic radius.

lock?

optional lock?: Object3D<Object3DEventMap>;

Defined in: experiments/star-field/engine/types.ts:674

Inertial axis lock — a group between the orbit pivot and the mesh carrying rotation.z = tilt and counter-rotated on Y each frame. Without it the pivot's orbital Y-rotation precesses the spin axis with the body's position (perpetual solstice); the lock keeps the axis fixed in the parent frame so the terminator sweeps the hemispheres over the orbit — real seasons. Only set on directly orbiting tilted bodies.

rotor?

optional rotor?: Object3D<Object3DEventMap>;

Defined in: experiments/star-field/engine/types.ts:680

Differential-rotation subgroup — a volumetric galaxy's inner-disc Points cloud; tickFrame spins it at ROTOR_DIFF× the whole-disc rate so the core laps the rim the way real rotation curves do.

clouds?

optional clouds?: Object3D<Object3DEventMap>;

Defined in: experiments/star-field/engine/types.ts:688

Cloud-deck shell — Earth's cloud sphere rides inside mesh so it inherits surface spin; with def.weather the deck is the procedural field (jets/storms/snow evolve in the shader via the shared fxTime uniform), and updateFx still adds its legacy differential drift for static-texture decks.

flares?

optional flares?: object[];

Defined in: experiments/star-field/engine/types.ts:694

Solar limb flares — prominence sprites from makeSolarFlares; updateFx scales/opacities them by solarWind × sin⁴(t·rate+phase) so eruptions breathe and spike outward when a storm hits.

Defined in: experiments/star-field/engine/types.ts:755

Interstellar-collapse glyph — a flat point-glow sprite riding the pivot beside the real mesh, plus its own pick proxy. updateLod shows them (and hides the sphere) once the camera passes SF_LOD.SOLAR_FAR so the whole solar tier reads as a single bright star like every other sun in the neighborhood. farGlyph?

optional farGlyph?: Object3D<Object3DEventMap>;

Defined in: experiments/star-field/engine/types.ts:766

Galactic-star far glyph — the flat point-glow sprite a point star wears at chart distances. updateLod hides it while the node's near-field group (real photosphere sphere + annulus halo + corona + flares, parked on detail) resolves on approach, so the star reads as an unresolvable point from range and as its spectral class up close.

nebula?

optional nebula?: SFNebulaFx;

Defined in: experiments/star-field/engine/types.ts:772

Living-nebula animation record — parked on the sprite's userData by makeNebulaSprite (SF_USER_NEBULA) and lifted here so updateFx can churn the depth layers each frame.

comet?

optional comet?: object;

Defined in: experiments/star-field/engine/types.ts:782

Comet tail/coma animation record — updateFx reads the live conic radius off center.position.x (frame.ts writes it for ecc orbits) and re-drives each tail's particle field between rMin (periapsis — full stream) and rMax (apoapsis — near-invisible stub), reproducing how sublimation scales with solar flux. Each Points layer carries its seeded grain field in userData.gasPts — the record only needs the object handles.
